rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah's legal material cannot establish that Mosaic law adopted Hammurabi: the Torah was lost in Babylonian captivity, later reconstructed by Ezra amid Babylonian legal customs, and nonrevealed laws may still contain sound rulings.
rows.anchor: كيف يحكم بأن الله أمضى في الشريعة الكليمية كثيرا من شرائع حمورابي

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu Basir reports from Imam al-Sadiq that the injustice mixed with faith means associationism; another transmission from Abu Basir says it means doubt.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قوله تعالى { الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم } قال هو الشرك

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Ayyashi transmits Abu Basir's report from Imam al-Sadiq identifying the people who mixed faith with injustice as the Kharijites and their followers.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال سألت عن قول الله الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Yaqub ibn Shuayb reports from Imam al-Sadiq that the injustice is misguidance and what exceeds it.
rows.anchor: وفيه عن يعقوب بن شعيب عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قوله ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports variously identify injustice as associationism, doubt, Kharijite belief, misguidance, or loyalty to the enemies of the Imams; this variety supports a general term with degrees suited to different levels of understanding.
rows.anchor: الظلم في الآية مطلق وهو في إطلاقه ذو مراتب بحسب درجات الأفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham grew up apart from his people's society; when he joined his father and found them worshipping idols, his pure nature, divinely guided by insight into the kingdom of all things, rejected their practice.
rows.anchor: كان إبراهيم عليه السلام في طفوليته إلى أوائل تمييزه يعيش في معزل من مجتمع قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham gently urged his father to abandon idols and follow monotheism, but his father rejected him, threatened stoning, and expelled him; Abraham answered respectfully and promised to pray for him.
rows.anchor: فأخذ يحاج أباه في عبادته الأصنام ويدعوه إلى رفضها وتوحيد الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham challenged both idol worshippers and people worshipping the sun, moon, and stars; after his public fame grew, he stayed behind during their festival and smashed the idols, sparing the largest as a rhetorical setup.
rows.anchor: وقد كان من جانب آخر يحاج القوم في أمر الأصنام ويحاج أقواما آخرين منهم يعبدون الشمس والقمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By telling the crowd to ask the largest idol whether it had smashed the others, Abraham forced them to admit the idols could not speak; he then exposed the irrationality of worshipping powerless objects.
rows.anchor: ليعقبه بقوله فاسألوهم أن كانوا ينطقون حتى يعترفوا بصريح القول بأنهم جمادات لا حياة لهم ولا شعور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the people chose to burn Abraham, God made the fire cool and safe; Abraham also defeated the king's evasion about life and death by challenging him to bring the sun from the west.
rows.anchor: فجعله الله بردا عليه وسلاما وأبطل كيدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After escaping the fire, Abraham preached pure monotheism; a small group believed, including Lot and his wife, and he left his hostile people with his wife and Lot for the Holy Land.
rows.anchor: ثم لما أنجاه الله من النار أخذ يدعو إلى الدين الحنيف دين التوحيد فآمن له شرذمة قليلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says Azar, whom Abraham called his father, was not his biological father; Abraham later received glad tidings of Ishmael, Isaac, and Jacob.
rows.anchor: وتبرأ هو من آزر الذي كان يدعوه أبا ولم يكن بوالده الحقيقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At God's command Abraham settled his young son Ishmael in barren Mecca; the settlement grew into a town, and father and son built the Kaaba, instituted pilgrimage rites, and Abraham proclaimed the pilgrimage to humanity.
rows.anchor: ثم بنى بها الكعبة البيت الحرام بمشاركة من إسماعيل وهي أول بيت وضع للناس من جانب الله مباركا وهدى للعالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's final narrated trial was God's command to sacrifice Ishmael; when both submitted, God confirmed Abraham's vision and substituted a great sacrifice.
rows.anchor: فلما أسلما وتله للجبين نودي أن يا إبراهيم قد صدقت الرؤيا وفداه الله سبحانه بذبح عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an's final account of Abraham includes prayers he made in Mecca, ending with his plea for forgiveness for himself, his parents, and believers on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: ربنا اغفر لي ولوالدي وللمؤمنين يوم يقوم الحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an repeatedly praises Abraham, describing his early wisdom, wholehearted submission, monotheism, intimacy with God, patience, repentance, gratitude, prophethood, and faithfulness; it details his virtues more than those of any other prophet.
rows.anchor: ولم يفصل القرآن الكريم في نعوت أحد من الأنبياء والرسل المكرمين وكراماتهم ما فصل من نعوته وكراماته عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave Abraham major religious offices: leadership for humanity, scripture, wisdom, sovereignty, guidance, an enduring word among his descendants, prophethood in his line, and a good name among later generations.
rows.anchor: وجعلنا في ذريتهما النبوة والكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam preserves Abraham's religion through the Kaaba and pilgrimage rites, which reenact his settling of Ishmael and Hagar, the sacrifice trial, and Abraham's devotion and endurance.
rows.anchor: وشرع مناسك الحج وهي في حقيقة أعمال ممثلة لقصه إسكانه ابنه وام ولده وتضحية ابنه إسماعيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author traces the three monotheistic religions to Abraham: Judaism through Isaac, Christianity through Jesus, and Islam through Ishmael and Muhammad.
rows.anchor: فدين التوحيد في الدنيا أثره الطيب المبارك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abrahamic practices visible in Islam include prayer, almsgiving, pilgrimage, permitted livestock, disavowal of God's enemies, greeting, and ten bodily and head-related purity practices.
rows.anchor: ويشاهد في الإسلام من شرائعه الصلاة والزكاة والحج وإباحة لحوم الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's beneficial legacy includes sound beliefs and practices throughout human societies; the author then introduces the Torah's account of Abraham from Genesis 11–25 for comparison with the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: والبحث المستوفى يؤيد أن السنن الصالحة من الإعتقاد والعمل في المجتمع البشري

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: The Torah says Terah's family left Ur for Canaan, settled at Haran, and later Abraham left Haran at seventy-five after God's promise to make him a great nation and bless the peoples through him.
rows.anchor: قالت التوراة وقال الرب لأبرام اذهب من أرضك ومن عشيرتك ومن بيت أبيك

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: The Torah says Abraham traveled through Canaan building altars, then went to Egypt during famine and told Sarah to claim she was his sister; Pharaoh took her but later sent them away with wealth after divine plagues.
rows.anchor: فأوصى عليه رجالا فشيعوه وامرأته وكل ما كان له

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: The Torah says Abraham and Lot separated for lack of pasture; after Lot was captured in a war among regional kings, Abraham pursued and rescued him and his household, refused the king of Sodom's goods, and gave a tithe to Melchizedek.
rows.anchor: فكسرهم وتبعهم إلى " حوبة " التي عن شمال دمشق واسترجع كل الأموال

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: After ten childless years in Canaan, Sarai gave her Egyptian servant Hagar to Abraham as a wife, and Hagar conceived Ishmael.
rows.anchor: فأخذت ساراي امرأة أبرام هاجر المصرية جاريتها من بعد عشر سنين لإقامة أبرام في أرض كنعان

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: The Torah says Hagar fled Sarai, an angel told her to return and promised a son named Ishmael, who would be wild and opposed by others.
rows.anchor: فهربت هاجر منها فلقيها ملك فأمرها بالرجوع إلى سيدتها وأخبرها أنها ستلد ولدا ذكرا

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: At ninety-nine, Abram was renamed Abraham and received a covenant for himself and his descendants, including Canaan and circumcision; Ishmael was circumcised at thirteen.
rows.anchor: فلا يدعى اسمك بعد أبرام بل يكون اسمك إبراهيم لأني أجعلك أبا لجمهور من الأمم

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: The Torah says Sarah would bear Isaac and that God's covenant would pass through him, while Ishmael would also become a great nation; it recounts the visitors' promise of Isaac and their warning about Lot's people.
rows.anchor: ولكن عهدي أقيمه مع إسحاق الذي تلده سارة في هذا الوقت في السنة الآتية

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: The Torah says Abraham moved to Gerar and called Sarah his sister; Abimelech took her, then returned her with gifts after God rebuked him, while Abraham said she was his paternal half-sister.
rows.anchor: أن سارة اخته فأخذها الملك منه فعاتبها الرب في المنام

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: The Torah says Sarah bore Isaac when Abraham was one hundred; later she demanded that Hagar and Ishmael be expelled, and God assured Abraham that Ishmael too would become a nation and protected them in the wilderness.
rows.anchor: فقال الله لإبراهيم لا يقبح في عينيك من أجل الغلام ومن أجل جاريتك

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: The Torah identifies Isaac as the son God commanded Abraham to offer at Moriah; Isaac asked where the sacrificial lamb was, and Abraham replied that God would provide it.
rows.anchor: خذ ابنك وحيدك الذي تحبه إسحاق واذهب إلى أرض المريا وأصعده هناك محرقة

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: In the Torah's account, an angel stopped Abraham from killing Isaac and a ram replaced him; God swore to multiply Abraham's descendants and bless all nations through them.
rows.anchor: فذهب إبراهيم وأخذ الكبش وأصعده محرقة عوضا عن ابنه

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: The Torah then recounts Abraham's later marriage and sons, Sarah's death, and Abraham's death at 175, with Isaac and Ishmael burying him in the cave of Machpelah.
rows.anchor: ثم موت إبراهيم وهو ابن مائة وخمس وسبعين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the Torah's summary of Abraham's life in Genesis 11–25; the author invites critical comparison with the Qur'an and begins arguing that the account omits Abraham's early struggles against his people.
rows.anchor: فهذه خلاصة قصص إبراهيم عليه السلام وتاريخ حياته المورد في التوراة سفر التكوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah's omission of Abraham's early debates, the Kaaba, its sacred sanctuary, and pilgrimage reflects an Israelite bias; it catalogs his altars elsewhere and belittles Ishmael as a wild, expelled archer.
rows.anchor: وليس إهمال ذكره إلا لنزعة إسرائيلية من كتاب التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah's account that Abraham twice offered Sarah as his sister to rulers for protection and reward is incompatible with his prophetic dignity; its claim that elderly Sarah was taken as a wife is also implausible.
rows.anchor: وأيسر ما في هذا الكلام أن يكون إبراهيم وحاشا مقام الخليل يعرض زوجته سارة لأمثال فرعون وأبي مالك

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report in both Sahih collections says Abraham named three statements as lies: that he was sick, that the largest idol did it, and that Sarah was his sister; the ruler seized Sarah, then released her and gave her Hajar.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال لم يكذب إبراهيم النبي عليه السلام قط إلا ثلاث كذبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The long intercession narration is transmitted through numerous routes and authorities, including Anas, Abu Hurayra, Hudhayfa, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masud, and others; Abraham declines to intercede because he recalls three alleged lies.
rows.anchor: وهو حديث طويل فيه أن أهل الموقف يأتون الأنبياء واحدا بعد واحد يسألونهم الشفاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects treating Abraham's statements as actual lies: if they were only figurative evasions done for religion, they would be merits, so they could not explain his refusal of intercession; prophets cannot lie because that would destroy trust in their revelations.
rows.anchor: أن ذلك مما لا يجوز على الأنبياء عليهم السلام قطعا لاستيجابه سلب الوثوق عن إخباراتهم وأحاديثهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says Abraham's words need not be lies: he may truly have been ill, and the statement that the chief idol did it was a rhetorical challenge that made the idolaters admit their idols could not speak.
rows.anchor: لا سبيل إلى عده كذبا فإنه كلام موضوع مكان التبكيت مسوق لإلزام الخصم على الاعتراف ببطلان مذهبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Abraham a habitual liar contradicts God's praise of him as a truthful prophet; the author appeals to the Qur'an's depiction of his integrity and argues such claims cannot fit his station.
rows.anchor: واذكر في الكتاب إبراهيم إنه كان صديقا نبيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports from the Imams preserve the basic story while clearing Abraham of lies and anything unworthy of his sanctity; al-Kafi relates a detailed account from Imam al-Sadiq.
rows.anchor: ومن أجمع ما يتضمن قصة الخليل عليه السلام ما في الكافي

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Imam al-Sadiq's al-Kafi report says Abraham was born in Kuthar, lived initially by natural disposition, married his cousin Sarah, and prospered after she gave him her considerable property.
rows.anchor: سمعت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام يقول أن إبراهيم عليه السلام كان مولده بكوثار

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: The al-Kafi report says Nimrod tried to burn Abraham, but he emerged unharmed; Nimrod expelled him, and Abraham secured release of his property by demanding compensation for his time in the country.
rows.anchor: وإن إبراهيم عليه السلام لما كسر أصنام نمروذ وأمر به نمروذ فأوثق وعمل له حيرا

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: The report says Abraham left for Syria with Lot and Sarah, hiding her in a chest; when a customs officer discovered her, Abraham said she was his wife and cousin and refused to open the chest without compensation.
rows.anchor: فخرج إبراهيم ومعه لوط لا يفارقه وسارة، وقال لهم إني ذاهب إلى ربي سيهدين

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: In al-Kafi's account, Abraham prayed that the king's hand be restrained from Sarah; after it was restored and restrained a second time, the king acknowledged Abraham's God and asked to give Sarah a maid, Hajar.
rows.anchor: وقال اللهم احبس يده عن حرمتي وابنة خالتي فلم تصل يده إليها

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: The report says God told Abraham to walk behind the earthly ruler and honor his authority, since the earth needs a ruler whether righteous or wicked; the king was impressed by God's gentleness and generosity.
rows.anchor: ولا بد من إمرة في الأرض برة أو فاجرة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: The al-Kafi narrative says Abraham settled near Syria, left Lot farther south, and, when Sarah had no child, bought Hagar from her; Hagar bore Ishmael.
rows.anchor: ثم أن إبراهيم عليه السلام لما أبطأ عليه الولد قال لسارة لو شئت لبعتني هاجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against the Torah's identification of Isaac as the intended sacrifice, the author favors Ishmael: the Meccan settlement, Kaaba, Hajj, and associated trials of Hagar and Ishmael support this reading.
rows.anchor: كل ذلك تؤيد كون الذبيح هو إسماعيل دون إسحاق عليهما السلام

rows.speaker: إنجيل برنابا
rows.claim: The Gospel of Barnabas portrays Jesus rebuking Jews for naming Isaac as the sacrifice and says Ishmael was Abraham's firstborn, commanded for offering.
rows.anchor: وقع في إنجيل برنابا أن المسيح لام اليهود ووبخهم على قولهم بأن الذبيح هو إسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'anic sequence in al-Saffat strongly identifies the sacrificed son as Ishmael: it gives glad tidings of a forbearing boy, narrates the sacrifice, and only afterward announces Isaac.
rows.anchor: وأما القرآن فإن آياته كالصريحة في كون الذبيح هو إسماعيل عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first glad tidings in al-Saffat concern a son distinct from the later-announced Isaac, and the first son is the one taken for sacrifice; Shia reports identify him as Ishmael, while Sunni reports differ, and Ishmael's view matches the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: أن الذبيح هو الذي ذكر الله سبحانه البشارة به في قوله

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari reports early disagreement but favors Isaac as the intended sacrifice: Abraham asked for a righteous son before Hagar, the Qur'an elsewhere names only Isaac as the promised boy, and Jacob may have been born before the command; the ram's horns could have been brought to Mecca.
rows.anchor: قال الطبري في تاريخه اختلف السلف من علماء أمة نبينا محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author objects that Abraham asked generally for a righteous son, not specifically a son from Sarah, so al-Tabari's argument from the timing of Hagar's arrival does not establish Isaac.
rows.anchor: فسأل ربه الولد، ولم يسأل أن يرزقه ذلك من سارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects al-Tabari's analogy to other announcements: the passage announces a forbearing son, narrates the sacrifice, then separately announces Isaac, so the first son must be Ishmael; historians agree Ishmael was born first.
rows.anchor: فقد بشر إبراهيم عليه السلام قبل اسحاق بولد له آخر وليس إلا اسماعيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author argues the Torah's chronology conflicts with its own story: Ishmael was fourteen years older than Isaac, yet the expulsion narrative depicts him as a nursing child; this accords with the transmitted account known to the author.
rows.anchor: ولا يرتاب الناظر المتدبر في القصة أن إسماعيل كان عندئذ صبيا مرضعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an gives substantial attention to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, and both lines of descendants; the Torah centers Isaac and Israel, disparages Ishmael, and contradicts itself about his status.
rows.anchor: فإنها تقصر الخبر عنه بما يتعلق بإسحاق وشعب إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author presents and rejects an orientalist claim that Muhammad added Abraham's ties to Ishmael, the Kaaba, and Arab Islam in Medinan surahs after losing Jewish support in Mecca.
rows.anchor: أن القرآن في سوره المكية لا يتعرض لشأن إبراهيم واسماعيل عليهما السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The orientalist accusation that the Qur'an adjusted its message to court Jews or others is false; after the Hijra, Jewish topics and detailed laws naturally appear in verses responding to new events.
rows.anchor: باحث متدبر يشاهد أن القرآن الكريم لم يداهن مشركا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Meccan chapter already links Abraham, Ishmael, the sanctuary in Mecca, and prayer, disproving the claim that these connections first appeared in Medinan revelations.
rows.anchor: فيكذبه قوله تعالى في سورة إبراهيم وهي مكية فيما حكاه من دعاء إبراهيم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an rejects the claim that Abraham was Jewish or Christian, affirming that he was a monotheist submitting to God and not an idolater.
rows.anchor: ما كان إبراهيم يهوديا ولا نصرانيا ولكن كان حنيفا مسلما وما كان من المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that Abraham could only have debated celestial worshippers after reaching Harran is, the author concludes, a problem for his earlier interpretation of the passage rather than for the Qur'an itself.
rows.anchor: وهذا في الحقيقة إشكال على التفسير الذي تقدم إيراده في بيان الآيات لا على أصل الكتاب
